name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
summary: Founded by Cyrus the Great, the Achaemenid Empire united the Near East from the Nile and Aegean to the Indus River. Famous for cultural and religious tolerance, the satrapy system, the 2,700 km Royal Road postal relay, qanat underground irrigation, and Persepolis.
keyFacts: Cyrus Cylinder (539 BCE)—landmark declaration of religious and cultural restoration
Royal Road courier system ("neither snow nor rain..."), gold Daric coinage, and Persepolis
Qanat subterranean aquifer channels turning arid plateaus into gardens (pairidaeza → "paradise")

name: Parthian & Sassanid Persian Empires
summary: For nine centuries, Parthian heavy cataphracts and horse-archers and the Sassanid Empire served as Rome and Byzantium’s sole superpower equal, connecting the Silk Road and founding the medical-philosophical Academy of Gondishapur.
keyFacts: Taq Kasra (Arch of Ctesiphon)—still the world’s largest unreinforced brick vault
Academy of Gondishapur (center of medicine, astronomy, and Greek-Sanskrit-Persian translation)

name: Seljuk, Timurid & Safavid → Modern Iran
summary: From Seljuk astronomy (Omar Khayyam’s Jalali calendar, more accurate than the Gregorian) and Persian poetry (Ferdowsi, Rumi, Hafez, Saadi) to Timurid Samarkand and Safavid Isfahan ("Isfahan is half the world").
keyFacts: Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh, Rumi’s Masnavi, and Omar Khayyam’s algebra & Jalali solar calendar
